surfaces.part: leaf canopy (main volume, lit top and darker underside)

answer.evidence: The canopy is the main body. Its width profile widens from 6 px at row 2 to 28 px at rows 13-15, then narrows to 19 px at row 28 and 10 px at row 30. This gives a rounded, ellipse-like mass. The upper rows (about 2-16) are lit light green and read as the top of the foliage seen from above. Rows 21-29 are darker green and near-black, forming a shaded underside that reads as eave shadow above the trunk. The trunk (rows 30-43, 5-7 px wide) and the root flare (rows 44-47, up to 25 px wide) form a front face of 3+ rows. There is no flat front-edge line, because the organic shape is shaded instead, but the volume reads as 3/4 view rather than a flat elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, compact tree with a round canopy in about 4 greens, a thin trunk and a few grass dots. Its dark edge pixels are tinted dark green and brown (0% neutral), so the outline is a dark material tone, not a sticker line. Its measured 10 visible tones per tile are well below the references' 26 and 29, and raw colours per tile are 11 against about 108. Beodeul canopies have distinct leaf clumps with bright highlight leaves, forked branches showing through, and a flared root base. The candidate's canopy is a soft, fairly uniform mass with only light speckle, the trunk is a simple stick, and the highlights are muted. There are no large flat fills (0% near-flat). The tree is clearly thinner and less detailed than the references at the same scale, so it fails on density and shading depth.
